meta.title: Dalibre — a calibre alternative for you and your AI agent
meta.description: Dalibre is a lightweight calibre alternative designed for both people and AI agents: a fast, native e-book manager that opens your existing calibre library, and lets your agent manage it and write plugins for it.
meta.ogAlt: Dalibre: a library for you, and your AI agent.

MCP server for AI agents such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Cursor
AI agents can write, try and install plugins over MCP

faq.lead: What Dalibre does, what it leaves to calibre, and how the two share a library.

items.a: Yes, for managing your e-book library. Dalibre does the everyday part of calibre (browsing, searching, editing metadata, getting books and sending them to your e-reader) in a native app that is {ratio}× smaller. Format conversion is in the works; calibre's e-book editor is out of scope.

items.q: Do I have to migrate my calibre library?
items.a: No. Dalibre reads and writes calibre's own library format (metadata.db, its folder layout and metadata.opf), so it opens the library you already have. Nothing to import, nothing to export.

items.q: Can I use Dalibre and calibre on the same library?
items.a: Yes. Both apps work on the same files, so you can open your library in either one, any day, and keep calibre for the jobs Dalibre doesn't do.

Not yet. We are working on it. Until then, keep using calibre on the same library to convert between EPUB, MOBI, AZW3 or PDF, or ask an AI agent connected over MCP: it can convert a book with calibre's ebook-convert and add the result to it.

items.q: How do I get books onto my e-reader?
items.a: Turn on sharing and Dalibre serves your library over OPDS on your Wi-Fi. Reading apps such as KOReader, Moon+ Reader, Thorium and KyBook browse it and download the books you pick. No cables, no cloud, no account.

items.q: Can AI agents use my library?
items.a: Yes. Turn on MCP and agents such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Cursor can search your library, edit metadata, add books and convert formats with the tools they already have. Only programs on your computer can connect, with a token, and Dalibre shows every call they make.

items.q: Can an AI agent write a Dalibre plugin for me?
items.a: Yes. Over MCP an agent can start a plugin from the template, add it to Dalibre, call it, read its results, logs and errors, and fix it until it works. Dalibre still asks you to allow the hosts the plugin reaches; the agent can't allow them for you.

items.q: Which platforms does Dalibre run on?
items.a: macOS, Windows and Linux. Dalibre is a single native binary written in Go: no webview, no bundled Python, no runtime to install.
No. Dalibre has its own plugins: small, sandboxed JavaScript modules that add places to get books and to look up metadata. Anyone can write one.
